question.worked_solution:
The "square of a difference" formula states that

$$
{n}^{2}-2an+{a}^{2}=(n-a)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
{n}^{2}-8n+16.
$$

First, we write the constant term as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}^{2}-8n+{4}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}^{2}-2\cdot 4n+{4}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of difference formula with $a=4.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(n-4)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
